newsitem.title: GERMANY: Norddeutsche chief positive on copper consumption.
newsitem.headline: Norddeutsche chief positive on copper consumption.

text.p: Global demand for copper products is satisfactory, and especially strong in Asia, Werner Marnette, chairman of German refiner Norddeutsche Affinerie AG (NA), said.
"Our sales of copper rod and semi-fabricated products have been encouraging in a competitive environment," he said in response to an enquiry.
"We are confident on the sales result for the (Oct/Sept 1996/97) season as European demand improves and German investments pick up."
Third country exports had been helped by a favourable currency equation, he added.
Tightness in cathodes -- reflected in LME stocks drawdowns by 1,125 on Wednesday and by 975 on Thursday -- was exacerbated by short supplies of Russian material, Marnette said.
LME copper set a fresh one-year high on Thursday as fundamentals remained strong, although there were signs of overbought conditions and looming supply additions in the second half of 1997.
But Marnette said he did believe in huge downside potential from supply gains later in 1997.
NA in 1995/96 produced 368,958 tonnes of cathodes while output of semis -- continuously cast billets and cakes -- amounted to 109,950 and coppper rod 227,940 tonnes.
